overview: Query logs land in Kafka → S3; a daily Spark job aggregates counts and builds a trie where each node stores its top-10. Serialized tries are loaded into suggestion servers (sharded by first letters); responses cached at CDN with short TTL.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative query vocabulary: 10M distinct queries, up to 10 prefixes each.
estimation.calculation: 10,000,000 × 10 = up to 100M prefix memberships before sharing/pruning.
estimation.result: Naively indexing every prefix multiplies storage and update work.
estimation.implication: Precompute top-K and prune long-tail prefixes; batch trie builds trade freshness for simpler serving.

entityDetails.purpose: Precomputed best queries per normalized prefix.
accessPatterns: Fetch the top suggestions in one lookup; publish a new ranking version.
constraints: Normalize case/locale consistently; bound prefixes and result count to prevent index explosion.

apiDetails.purpose: Return fast top suggestions for a prefix.
apiDetails.rationale: Debounce client requests and cache normalized-prefix results. Apply privacy filtering before publishing query logs.

failureCases.scenario: A ranking build fails or a stream updater falls behind
failureCases.handling: Keep serving the last complete version; publish builds with atomic version swaps. Monitor freshness, dedup replayed query events, and expire stale CDN results within the freshness budget.

alternatives: Use batch-built tries for very fast reads when daily staleness is acceptable. Use streaming prefix sorted sets for fresher trends, accepting higher update work, prefix cardinality and score-decay complexity.
